item.title: Vintage Ansonia defense, Taylor's big day lead Chargers past Naugatuck for share of NVL title
item.description: Ansonia's Zaire Moore (76) hoists the Shortell-Lucas Trophy with teammates following their win over Naugatuck during their annual Thanksgiving Day football game at Naugatuck High School Thursday, November 26, 2026. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) NAUGATUCK - Just in case anyone had forgotten how dominant the Ansonia football program can be, the Chargers issued a reminder Thursday at Naugatuck's Craig Peters Field. Playing with tremendous physicality and aggression on defense and leaning heavily on a supremely talented running back offensively, the Chargers earned a share of the Naugatuck Valley League championship by beating Naugatuck 32-0. Tymir Taylor rushed for 261 yards on 33 carries, including touchdown runs of 1, 2, 19 and 55 yards to give Ansonia a ton of momentum heading into Tuesday's state playoffs. "It means a lot, beating an undefeated team that beat a team (Holy Cross) that beat us," Taylor said. "It definitely means a lot to come here and put those points on the board like we did today. We're looking really good right now, just getting ready for our first opponent." Ansonia improved to 9-1 and will host a Class SS quarterfinal Tuesday, Dec. 1. Naugatuck also finished 9-1 and will host a Class L quarterfinal. Their opponents will be determined when the CIAC releases the official seeds and pairings Friday. Ansonia coach Shane Kingsley said he felt like a great performance was coming from his team from the moment the Chargers stepped onto the field on Thursday morning. "I felt it from the kids in warmups," Kingsley said. "They had that Ansonia look about them. We told our offensive line they were going to have to control the line of scrimmage. We played Ansonia football today. We ran the ball, ran to the football aggressively on defense and tackled, and the results were what we wanted." The result of such focused play was that the outcome of the game never seemed in doubt from the time Taylor scored his first touchdown. The Ansonia defense was unyielding, and the Chargers' offensive line gave Taylor all that he needed to make big plays. "I think Tymir Taylor has become a complete back this year," Kingsley said. "Last year he might've gotten caught on a few of those runs, but not this year. He's breaking tackles at the line of scrimmage, and when he gets daylight, he's gone. He's worked really hard, and I'm happy he's seeing the results." The Ansonia defense complemented him perfectly, shutting down the very talented Naugy duo of running back/QB Qwentarvous Lee and running back Brandon Andoh. Lee finished with 56 yards rushing and Andoh with 50. "From the moment we came in for the pregame walkthru, we were locked in and ready to go," defensive lineman Zaire Moore said. "It was definitely the aggression and the mindset, and the things they'd been talking about over the internet. It was crazy. We just had to show them who rules." item.title: Here are 4 ways OKC Thunder can snap out of current 3-game losing streak
item.description: For two entire regular seasons, the Oklahoma City Thunder never experienced a three-game losing streaks. Now, they've experienced two of those over the last month. Injuries have finally done a number on the once-hopeful title favorite. A month into the Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) world, they're clinging onto pure survival. For the first time since the Thunder experienced one of the darkest days in their franchise history, their postseason spot is starting to look a little murky to forecast. Once a foregone conclusion, OKC enters Thanksgiving in 11th place in the Western Conference standings. The Thunder started the year an admirable 8-2. Since then, they've lost seven of nine games. The latest painted a similar picture to most of their defeats. They kept it close, but no dice, in an NBA Cup loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . So, now what? As surreal as it sounds, the Thunder still have 63 regular-season matchups to go. Here are four quick fixes to their current three-game losing streak: Ajay Mitchell becomes more consistent When the Thunder first experienced their season-altering injuries to Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace, most penciled Mitchell in as a benefactor. With three of their four best players out, he was pushed to the front of the line. His temporary promotion includes him going from a Sixth Man to OKC's second-best scorer. So far, it's been a wild ride. Before he dropped 25 points over the daunting Timberwolves, Mitchell had struggled in his last handful of contests. He went on a seven-game streak failing to crack 20 points and on poor efficinecy. That obviously needs to change. Out of pure necessity, too. He hasn't taken full advantage of the opportunity in front of him, per se, but has a couple of more months to do so. Start Alex Caruso Sometimes, the biggest solutions are the simplest ones. Even through their dire health situation, the Thunder have remained stubborn on Caruso's role. It's been mostly bench-exclusive. Sans one start. Run of the mill for his three seasons in OKC. In that time, he's started four whopping games total. Quite the juxtaposition from what his role was on the Chicago Bulls . But considering the Thunder have habitually fallen behind with slow first quarters, can they afford to keep Caruso in his bench role? I just don't think so. He's a basketball impact deity. There's a reason why all of the advanced metrics absolutely love him. He has an eye-popping plus-33 point swing in his on-off splits. I get wanting to reserve that tsunami number to keep your second unit afloat, but that's irrelevant if you're always behind to start games. item.title: Rafael Nadal reveals what he told his uncle during the rain delay in the 2008 Wimbledon final with Roger Federer
item.description: In 2008, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer delivered one of the greatest tennis matches of all time. Nadal and Federer met in the Wimbledon final for the third consecutive season that year, and this time the Spaniard came out on top after a thrilling five-setter that lasted four hours and 48 minutes. The match had started at 2 pm local time, but it was in danger of having to be postponed until the next day due to rain delays. A second rain delay occurred at around 8 pm after Federer had rallied from two sets down to force a decider, and when the players returned to the court, darkness had started to settle in. At this point, there was no roof on Centre Court. During that interruption, Nadal had a conversation with his uncle and coach, Toni Nadal, which he recalled in a recent interview with Brut . Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls what happened in the 2008 Wimbledon final “For me, the 2007 final of Wimbledon loss, I think helped me to be ready for the 2008 final,” said Nadal. The 22-time Grand Slam champion had fallen to Federer in the championship match at the All England Club in 2006 and 2007. He lost in four sets in 2006, but forced Federer to a fifth set in 2007. Recalling his conversation with Toni in 2008, Nadal said: “I would say, okay, I can lose, but I will not fail. That’s true. I said, okay, no worries. I can lose. Maybe he beat me, but I’m not going to lose. That’s what I told him [Toni] on the last rain delay. “Because I was in a tricky situation. I was two sets up. Then I lost the next two. I lost two match points in the fourth. So the match was not in my way in that moment. But I said, okay, I mean, I am closer than ever to winning Wimbledon. So it’s not the moment to fail. I said to my uncle, no worries. I will not fail. Maybe he beat me because he’s very good, but I will be there all the time.” Having squandered two championship points in the fourth set, Nadal ultimately triumphed 6–4, 6–4, 6–7 (5-7), 6–7 (8-10), 9–7 to hoist his first of two Wimbledon titles. Nadal made a habit of winning throughout his illustrious career, but always dealt with losses well. “In some way, the loss needs to be accepted to play,” he said. “Because when you play, especially when you play in a sport like tennis, that every day is one against the other, one will lose. And maybe it’s you that day. “And especially, even imagine when you play against Federer or Djokovic or these kinds of players. You go on court knowing that even if you play well, you can lose. So it’s not about talking about that or have fear about losing. It’s about, you know, that’s there. But you can’t think about that. item.title: Tiger Woods Legal Setback Is Just Noise Before The Hero Return
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tiger Woods’ apparel brand faces a legal setback just as he prepares for his competitive return, yet the golf world remains ready to welcome him back. Davis Love III confirmed that tour leaders view Woods playing as the best thing for the sport. The 15-time major champion will tee it up at the Hero World Challenge next week in the Bahamas after a long layoff. Woods has not played a tournament since July 2024 at Royal Troon. He underwent back surgery in 2025 and addressed a prescription painkiller addiction earlier this year. Despite these struggles, reports from HITC via Yahoo indicate he has reached “crazy” ball speeds during practice sessions. The tour is eager to see if his body can handle the pressure of competition again. The Tour Needs The Buzz Back PGA Tour chiefs are not hiding their desire to see Woods compete. While speaking on the Fully Equipped Podcast, Davis Love III revealed the sentiment inside the tournament office. He stated, “In PGA Tour talks, you know, talks around our tournament office, the best thing for the PGA Tour, or the Champions Tour, is for Tiger Woods to play.” The tour knows that Woods brings a level of attention no other player can match. Love compared the situation to Michael Jordan’s return to the NBA. “You know, we miss him, we miss the buzz that he gets,” Love said. “You know, Michael Jordan left for a while, and then he came back to the NBA.” This comparison highlights just how much the game has felt his absence over the last two years. The light he shines on other players like Rory McIlroy and Blades Brown is something the tour cannot ignore. A Controlled Environment For A Comeback The Hero World Challenge offers the specific setting Woods needs to test his limits. Love described the event as the ideal spot for a comeback attempt. “The Hero is the perfect place, you know? It’s a controlled environment,” Love said. This setup allows Woods to play without the overwhelming pressure of a full-field major championship. Experts suggest a schedule of about 10 events for Woods in 2027, including the majors. This approach prevents him from pushing his body or mind too hard too soon. The Father Son Classic is another controlled event that could spur him on to join the Champions Tour later.

item.title: Levski Sofia coach says Marseille fan clashes 'unacceptable'
item.description: A blood-stained Levski Sofia supporter tries to escape from Marseille supporters ahead of the Europa League match (Justine MEDDAH) Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez said violent clashes between fans of the Bulgarian club and Marseille supporters ahead of their Europa League game on Thursday were "unacceptable for football". The lead-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by incidents in the stands between the two sets of supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered. Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Genesio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf

item.title: Ohio State football loses commitment from 5-star defensive end DJ Jacobs
item.description: Ohio State has lost a verbal commitment from DJ Jacobs , a five-star defensive end who is considered one of the highest ranked prospects in country in the recruiting class for 2027. Jacobs told On3 on Nov. 26 that he had decommitted from the Buckeyes. He had been committed for nearly a year. The decision comes six days before the start of the early signing period, which begins on Dec. 2 and allows prospects to solidify their plans. Jacobs is the No. 2 overall prospect and top-ranked edge rusher in his class, according to composite rankings from 247Sports. He had 95 tackles and 12 sacks this year as a senior at Blessed Trinity Catholic High School in the northern Atlanta suburb of Roswell. Georgia, Miami and Tennessee have all been linked to Jacobs late in this recruiting cycle. His father, David, was a defensive lineman at Georgia from 1999-2002. The move by Jacobs leaves the Buckeyes with 22 verbal commitments in the class, which was just outside the top-five at No. 6 in the composite rankings behind Notre Dame, Texas A&M, Miami, Oregon Florida on Nov. 26. The Buckeyes have two other five-star defensive linemen who are committed for 2027 between Marcus Fakatou and Wyatt Smith. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X. item.title: Steelers Owner Makes Major Decision on Mike McCarthy’s Future After Aaron Rodgers’ Rant
item.description: Steelers owner sticks by Mike McCarthy. Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers will be sticking with Mike McCarthy as their head coach. The Steelers released future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers after he was benched and then took shots at head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is off to a 6-4 start and is holding onto a playoff spot. Pittsburgh Steelers Owner Sticks by Mike McCarthy Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. After Rodgers went on a lengthy rant about McCarthy and why he isn’t a good coach, Steelers owner Art Rooney II is sticking by the coach. Rooney broke his silence on the incident. He spoke to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Gazette and said he will be sticking with McCarthy as the Steelers head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney said Rodgers never once said anything about McCarthy and his health to him during his tenure with the Steelers. So, Rooney admits he is disappointed with how Rodgers handled the situation and went public with it all. “I’m disappointed the way it came out,” Rooney said. “We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll. We had high expectations. It’s easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” McCarthy is in his first year as the Steelers head coach. Rooney Believes McCarthy Protected Rodgers Not only does Rooney plan to stick with McCarthy, but he believes the head coach did a good job defending the quarterback. Rooney believes McCarthy took bullets for Rodgers when the offense was struggling, instead of the blame going to the quarterback. “The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called. Particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.” The Steelers will now turn their attention to the Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon. item.title: Cesc Fàbregas speaks on potential Barcelona return
item.description: Cesc Fàbregas speaks on potential Barcelona return Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas has this week spoken out on the possibility of taking his talents back to his former stomping grounds at La Liga champions Barcelona. This of course comes amid ongoing speculation tipping the Spaniard as a potential long-term replacement for Hansi Flick in Catalunya’s capital. Fàbregas and Flick’s contracts with their respective clubs are due to expire in the summer of 2028. The former, meanwhile, has long been earning for himself a reputation as one of European football’s standout up-and-coming tacticians. On the bench at Italian outfit Como, Fàbregas has defied the odds en route to establishing his club as one of Serie A’s leading lights. Boasting Barcelona DNA courtesy of his time spent at La Masia, the former Blaugrana midfielder is in turn considered an almost inevitable future arrival back at the Camp Nou. Speaking during an appearance in front of the media this week, Fàbregas was therefore drawn on this very topic. And the Spaniard went on to provide an in-depth response, as follows: “I’m one of those who live day by day. Thinking about the future usually doesn’t get you anywhere. “I’m from there, I grew up at that club, and I know everyone, but I’ve never liked thinking too far ahead. The times I have, it hasn’t gone well. Life is like piloting a plane; you never know when it’s going to brake. That’s why we have to try to enjoy ourselves. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Being one of the best scorers in the NBA doesn’t necessarily mean you’re one of the best three-level scorers. Just look at Giannis Antetokounmpo , who’s been putting up 30 PPG for years without needing much of a three-point shot, or Stephen Curry, who can go for 40 points without even touching the paint (though I’d say he’s definitely inside this category). When we talk about three-level scoring, we’re looking at guys who can get their points in three different areas of the court. The first one is inside the paint, whether that’s through post-ups, layups, dunks, or floaters. The second is the mid-range, where we get most of those pull-up jumpers and fadeaways, and the third is obviously scoring from beyond the arc. What makes these guys so difficult to guard is that taking away one shot doesn’t take them out of the game. Go under a screen, and they’ll pull up from three. Play too high, and they’ll get to the rim. Drop your big man too far into the paint, and they’ll get an open jumper from the elbow. For this ranking, we’re looking at scoring production from each area, shooting efficiency, volume, and how good these players are at creating their own shots. We’re also putting more weight on what they’ve been doing this season rather than their glory or reputation, with all stats coming from the 2026-27 regular season. With that in mind, here are the 10 best three-level scorers in the NBA right now. 10. But at 38 years old, the Houston Rockets forward is taking just 13.5 shots per game, his lowest volume since coming into the NBA. The efficiency is still there, though. Durant is shooting 50.8% from the field, 39.7% from three, and 88.1% from the free-throw line, good for a 64.9% true shooting mark. He’s also making 55.6% of his two-point attempts, so it’s not like he’s suddenly having problems scoring inside the arc. Durant ranks sixth in the NBA in mid-range scoring at 4.5 points per game, which accounts for around 21% of his entire scoring production. He’s still getting to those same spots around the elbows, shooting over smaller defenders in the post, and pulling up from pretty much anywhere inside the three-point line. He’s getting fewer opportunities to attack the rim and letting guys like Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson handle more of the scoring this year. item.title: Great Britain overcome Germany to make first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019
item.description: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched victory for Great Britain in a difficult tie against Germany to seal passage to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019. It has been an eventful week for Patten, with his doubles partner Harri Heliovaara sharing his shock and dismay at the Briton’s surprise decision to end their highly successful partnership after three grand slam titles together, only a few days after they were crowned year-end world No 1s. Patten will compete with Skupski, this year’s Australian and US Open champion, in 2027 and the pair immediately demonstrated their potential with an assured victory in the winner-takes-all doubles tie against Germany. The pair beat seasoned doubles players Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-2 7-6(6) in Bologna after world Cameron Norrie edged out Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3 3-6 6-2 and British No 1 Arthur Fery was beaten 6-3 6-2 by world No 1 Alexander Zverev . Krawietz and Puetz are the most successful doubles pair in German Davis Cup history having won 18 of their previous 20 matches but Patten and Skupski started brilliantly before edging a tight second set. Earlier on Thursday Norrie battled past the in-form Struff, who is ranked 13 places higher at 39, saving four break points in a crucial game at 2-2 in the deciding set before rattling off 18 of the final 21 points of the contest. Norrie said: “I knew that my match was going to be a really important one, knowing we’re playing against Germany with Sascha Zverev. I knew I had to take care of this one. Norrie dug deep to put GB ahead (Getty) “I tried to be aggressive those two games from 2-1 up and I overplayed a little bit. But I stuck to it in that game at 2-2 being 0-40 down and then I just found my tempo. “I locked it in. I didn’t really remember the end of the match. I made every return, every ball, I was moving him side to side and I could see him struggling.” Fery had lost to Zverev twice this year, in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again in Vienna, and their head-to-head remained lopsided as the German needed just 70 minutes to level the best-of-three tie. Germany boast the top-ranked singles player (Getty) 24-year-old Fery said: “It’s tough. He’s serving so well, hitting hard from the back of the court so not much time from my end to adjust. It’s obviously not easy, just try and do some different things. It feels a little bit like it’s all on his racket. “He’s a style of player that I struggle to play against. It’s positive, I’ve played him three times this year. If you’d told me that on January 1, it would have been a good thing.” GB now face a semi-final tie against Spain, led by Carlos Alcaraz , who beat Austria later on Thursday. Their star player was rested having been lined up to partner Marcel Granollers in the doubles tie, which was not needed after Daniel Merida beat Joel Schwaerzler 6-4 6-4 ​and world No 10 Rafael Jodar edged past ‌Jurij Rodionov 2-6 6-0 6-1.

item.description: Leeds United Chase French Striker Rennes Could Sell: Is £39m Worth It? Leeds United and Everton are reportedly targeting Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul, according to Sport Witness . The 26-year-old France international scored 20 goals and provided five assists in Ligue 1 last season, then added seven in eight league appearances this term, four of them penalties. Rennes extended his contract to 2030 in June, yet the report says they are preparing for a January or summer exit. Transfermarkt values him at €45m, roughly £39m. Eliezer Mayenda, a €22m (about £19m) signing, is struggling, so Rennes are already scouting Rosenborg’s Amin Chiakha as a replacement in attack. Lepaul’s strengths and weaknesses FotMob ‘s data shows a penalty-box finisher. His 29 shots have produced 16 on target and 5.80 expected goals, and he ranks in the 95th percentile among forwards for goals. The weaknesses are just as clear. He wins 40.9% of his aerial duels and 37.8% of all duels, and sits in the third percentile for defensive contributions. Only three of his seven goals this season came from open play. Where Leeds need help Leeds scored only 10 goals in their first ten league games before beating Chelsea 4-1 last Saturday to reach 17 points from 11. Noah Okafor scored twice there and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, 29, converted a penalty, yet the striker missed 19 big chances in the Premier League last season, according to FotMob. Farke’s back three and two strikers need forwards who press, and Calvert-Lewin has led the Premier League for pressures applied since the start of last season. Lepaul’s defensive numbers would test that. Should Leeds United pay £39m for Lepaul? ISTANBUL, TURKEY – AUGUST 2: Anthony Rouault of Rennes interacts with his teammate Esteban Lepaul during the during the pre-season friendly match between Galatasaray SK and Rennes at Rams Park Stadium on August 2, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) No, at least not in January and not at £39m or more. Rennes can keep him in Europa League football on a contract until 2030, and TEAMtalk reports Everton lead the chase. Everton have only Thierno Barry as a senior centre-forward, but Leeds face no such shortage. Their problem is conversion, which makes Lepaul tempting, yet he created just seven chances in 562 minutes and would not help Farke’s pressing. Calvert-Lewin started each of Leeds ‘ first ten league games, and Okafor is scoring, so Lepaul would arrive as a rotation option at a starter’s price. A cheaper, pressing-minded forward would suit the back three better. Summer is the sensible window, when Rennes may have Chiakha in place and Calvert-Lewin’s age gives succession a stronger case. item.title: Boxing chiefs to assess Fury before Joshua fight following schizophrenia comments
item.description: The British Boxing Board of Control will assess Tyson Fury ahead of his hotly anticipated bout against Anthony Joshua following comments he made about hearing voices during a mental health episode. A new self-titled documentary about the 38-year-old, to be released on Netflix on Friday, goes into detail about his mental health struggles. He and his wife Paris recalled frightening episodes in which he heard voices threatening him and his family after he was hospitalised with a suspected heart attack in 2016. He said: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.” In the original version of the documentary, which has since been edited before release, Paris said he was “mild schizophrenic”, although he was not medically diagnosed. Doctors said he had experienced a severe anxiety attack. Paris clarified her comments to The Mirror on Thursday: “Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love.” The British Boxing Board of Control said it would evaluate the comments broadcast in the documentary before clearing Fury to box Joshua, with the fight scheduled for 11 December in Cardiff’s Principality Stadium . The board’s general secretary, Robert Smith, told BBC Sport : “We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. “I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly. “If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box.” He declined to comment on the specifics of the process, saying, “it's a medical matter”. The board’s regulations state that schizophrenia is among psychological conditions which “may preclude” a boxer from obtaining a first licence. An existing licence holder is subject to “such action as in [the board’s] absolute discretion it sees fit”.

item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Doug Nester in a preseason game against the New York Jets on Aug. 21, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers have elevated offensive lineman Doug Nester from the practice squad for the second straight week for the team’s Week 12 Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos. Nester was also elevated in Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles and made his NFL debut, appearing in four snaps of special teams. Nester will again replace guard Mason McCormick , who suffered a gruesome leg injury in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. McCormick was placed on injured reserve and is expected to miss at least the rest of the regular season. Spencer Anderson will likely make his second straight start at left guard. Steelers rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker (knee) will not suit up for Friday’s game. He had his 21-day practice window opened last week but was not activated off injured reserve. Nester originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Minnesota Vikings in 2024 after finishing his college career at West Virginia . He later landed with the Steelers and spent time on Pittsburgh’s practice squad over the last two seasons. The 6-foot-6, 306-pound lineman signed a reserve/future contract in January with the Steelers. A native of Kenya, West Virginia, first attended Virginia Tech for his first two collegiate seasons before transferring to WVU. Nester started 10 games as a true freshman at right guard for the Hokies in 2019 and seven more in 2020. After transferring to West Virginia, he stated every game in 2021 and 2022 at right guard, before moving to right tackle for his redshirt senior season in 2023. He appeared in 57 games between the two programs and made 52 starts. Steelers guard Doug Nester during an OTAs practice on May 29, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Nester participated in both the Hula Bowl and the East-West Shrine Game in the pre-draft process, with the Steelers scouting him heavily at the latter stop. Despite his size, Nester did not test well leading up the draft, running a 5.31-second 40-yard dash and posting just 19 reps on the bench press. item.title: Rater Confidential: Top 100 Courses in the U.S. takeaways
item.description: Oakmont, and its famous church pew bunkers, ranked 5th on the list. Fred Vuich/SI via Getty Images GOLF’s Top 100 course panelists are among the most respected and well-traveled course evaluators in the game. And with the recent release of GOLF’s Top 100 Courses in the U.S. ranking for 2026-27 , we asked a few of them to weigh in on some of the biggest talking points. What’s your biggest takeaway from GOLF’s newest Top 100 Courses in the U.S. list? Does anything stand out? Does anything surprise you? Jon Orszag: Three things stand out. First, the remarkable stability at the top. All 25 courses in today’s top 25 were there four years ago — and the top five are unchanged. Despite endless debates about individual courses, there’s a strong and sustained consensus about America’s very best golf architecture. Second, the impact of restorations. Some of the most exciting developments in American golf aren’t new courses at all, but rather Golden Age masterpieces brought back to life. Like great architecture of any kind, great golf architecture is timeless, and sometimes the best way to improve a golf course is to rediscover what made it great in the first place. Third, the list establishes today’s architectural Big Three (but really four people) — Coore & Crenshaw, Doak, and Hanse. Their original designs and restorations touch 60 of the Top 100, including 45 restorations. In terms of influence, they are this generation’s Golden Age giants — today’s Tillinghast, Ross, MacKenzie, and Macdonald/Raynor. Henry Shimp: I’m always interested to see how courses move in the 51-150 bucket, as those are often the ones making changes to move into that top 50. With a course like Yale, that clearly paid off big time . However, multiple courses saw renovation dollars yield a negative rankings ROI, such as Congressional, Olympic Lake and Scioto. In the same vein, it’s very interesting, and encouraging, to see courses like St Louis CC, Old Elm and Kittansett all make meaningful jumps by simply making small course improvements over time, yet no major restoration work. Michael Blackham: Thirty years after Sand Hills kicked off the modern building boom, the old guys are still winning. Thirty-eight of the top 50 are classic-era designs. Only Sand Hills and Friar’s Head crack the top 20, and Sand Hills is the only modern course in the top 10. Even one of the modern entries, the Lido, is a recreation of a 1917 Macdonald design. Some of today’s new courses are terrific, but the best architecture is still mostly a century old. The post Rater Confidential: Top 100 Courses in the U.S. takeaways appeared first on Golf .

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
